answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by routing every new identity through a single shared violet inlet whose aperture is modulated by a continuous hardware signal from a unique physical sensor. The inlet opens only after a sequential delay that lengthens with the number of recent admissions, measured on one global clock no farm can parallelize. An attacker must therefore pay increasing real-time and hardware cost for each extra identity; the 50th clone waits far longer than the first and cannot batch the proof.
